questions.question: At what time (approximately) (in PM) between 3 PM and 4 PM will the hour and minute hands of the clock be opposite to each other?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

The **hour hand** covers 360° in 12 hours.

Angular distance covered by the **hour hand** in 1 minute = 360 ÷ (12 × 60) = 0.5°

The **minute hand** covers 360° in 60 minutes.

Angular distance covered by the **minute hand** in 1 minute = 360 ÷ 60 = 6°

The **relative speed** between the two hands = 6° − 0.5° = 5.5° per minute.

For the hands of a clock to be **opposite** to each other, the angle between them must be **180°**.

__**Calculation:**__

At **3 PM**, the **minute hand** is at 12 (0°) and the **hour hand** is at 3 (90°).

To be **opposite**, the minute hand must first cover the 90° gap to meet the hour hand and then move 180° further to be exactly opposite.

Total relative angular distance to be covered = 90° + 180° = 270°

Time taken = Distance ÷ Relative speed

Time = 270 ÷ 5.5 = 270 ÷ (11/2)

Time = 540/11 minutes ≈ 49.09 minutes

The time is approximately 49 minutes past 3, which is **3:49 PM**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

The angle between the **hour hand** and **minute hand** is given by the formula:

Angle = |30H − (11/2)M|

Where **H** is hours and **M** is minutes.

Here, H = 3 and the hands are **opposite**, so Angle = 180°.

180 = |30 × 3 − 5.5 × M|

180 = |90 − 5.5M|

Since the minute hand is ahead of the hour hand to form a 180° angle after 3 PM:

180 = 5.5M − 90

180 + 90 = 5.5M

270 = 5.5M

M = 270 ÷ 5.5 = 540/11

M ≈ 49.09 minutes

Hence, the correct answer is **3:49**.

questions.question: A watch is 6 minutes slow at 7 AM. It gains 12 seconds every hour. When will it show the correct time (in PM) again?
questions.solution:
The watch is **6 minutes slow** at **7 AM**.

The gain rate of the watch = **12 seconds per hour**.

To show the correct time, the total gain required is **6 minutes**.

Converting the required gain into seconds:

6 minutes = 6 × 60 = **360 seconds**.

Now, calculate the number of hours required to gain 360 seconds:

Time = Total gain required ÷ Gain per hour

Time = 360 ÷ 12 = **30 hours**.

To find the time when the watch will be correct, we add **30 hours** to the starting time of **7 AM**:

7 AM + 24 hours = 7 AM (the following day)

7 AM + 6 hours = **1 PM** (the following day)

The watch will show the correct time at **1:00 PM**.

Hence, the correct answer is “**Option 1**”.

questions.question: Education was transferred from state List to concurrent List by:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**42nd Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976**, often referred to as the **Mini-Constitution**, brought about the most extensive changes to the Indian Constitution during the tenure of Prime Minister **Indira Gandhi**.
 
• One of the significant changes was the transfer of five subjects from the **State List** (List II) to the **Concurrent List** (List III) of the **Seventh Schedule**.
 
• These five subjects were **Education**, **Forests**, **Weights and Measures**, **Protection of Wild Animals and Birds**, and **Administration of Justice** (excluding the Supreme Court and High Courts).
 
• By moving **Education** to the **Concurrent List**, the amendment enabled both the **Parliament** and the **State Legislatures** to enact laws on the subject, though central legislation takes precedence in case of a conflict under **Article 254**.
 
• This shift was intended to ensure a **uniform national standard** and policy for education across all states in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **44th Amendment Act, 1978**:

 
 
• Passed by the **Janata Government** to nullify several distortions introduced by the 42nd Amendment.
 
• It is most notable for removing the **Right to Property** from the list of Fundamental Rights and making it a **Legal Right** under **Article 300A**.
 
 
 
• **52nd Amendment Act, 1985**:
 
 
• Commonly known as the **Anti-Defection Law**.
 
• It inserted the **Tenth Schedule** to prevent political defections by members of Parliament and State Legislatures.
 
 
 
• **86th Amendment Act, 2002**:
 
 
• Focused on the implementation of the **Right to Education**.
 
• It inserted **Article 21A**, making free and compulsory education for children between **6 and 14 years** a **Fundamental Right**.
 
• It also added a new **Fundamental Duty** under **Article 51A(k)** for parents or guardians to provide educational opportunities.

questions.question: Which Finance Commission was the first to recommend Goods and Services Tax compensation to states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**13th Finance Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **13th Finance Commission**, which was chaired by **Dr. Vijay Kelkar** and covered the award period from **2010 to 2015**, was the first to explicitly recommend a compensation package for states to facilitate the rollout of the **Goods and Services Tax (GST)**.
 
• The commission proposed a **GST Compensation Fund** with an initial corpus of **50,000 crore rupees** to provide a financial cushion for states that might experience revenue shortfalls during the transition to the new indirect tax regime.
 
• It introduced the concept of a **Grand Bargain**, emphasizing that the central government should provide fiscal incentives to states to encourage the adoption of a comprehensive and uniform **GST model** across the country.
 
• The commission argued that while GST would eventually increase the tax base and improve **economic efficiency** by creating a **common national market**, the immediate loss of state-level taxes like **VAT** and **Entry Tax** required a formal compensation mechanism.
 
• These recommendations laid the essential groundwork for the fiscal architecture that was later adopted under the **101st Constitutional Amendment Act**, which eventually brought GST into effect on **1st July 2017**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **12th Finance Commission**:

 
 
• Chaired by **Dr. C. Rangarajan** (2005–2010), this commission primarily focused on **fiscal consolidation** and incentivizing states to implement the **Value Added Tax (VAT)** system.
 
 
 
• **14th Finance Commission**:
 
 
• Led by **Y.V. Reddy** (2015–2020), it is significant for increasing the vertical devolution of central taxes to states from **32 percent to 42 percent**, providing greater fiscal autonomy to state governments.
 
 
 
• **15th Finance Commission**:
 
 
• Chaired by **N.K. Singh** (2021–2026), it addressed the post-GST fiscal landscape and maintained the devolution share at **41 percent**, accounting for the new status of **Jammu and Kashmir** and **Ladakh**.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Mandate**:
 
 
• The Finance Commission is a **Constitutional Body** established under **Article 280** of the Constitution of India to recommend the distribution of tax proceeds between the **Union and the States**.

questions.question: Mulk Raj Anand's novel Two Leaves and a Bud is based on the exploitation of workers in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tea plantations**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Two Leaves and a Bud** is a seminal novel written by **Mulk Raj Anand**, first published in **1937**. It serves as a scathing critique of the **British colonial administration** and the **capitalist exploitation** inherent in the plantation economy.
 
• The narrative is set in the **Macpherson Tea Estate** located in **Assam**, India. The title of the novel is a direct reference to the method of plucking the top **two leaves and a bud** from the tea plant, which yields the highest quality tea.
 
• The story revolves around the protagonist, **Gangu**, a displaced **Punjabi peasant** who is lured to the tea gardens by the false promise of a better life and high wages, only to find himself trapped in a system of **indentured labor** and debt bondage.
 
• Anand vividly depicts the **dehumanizing conditions** faced by the workers, including poor sanitation, physical abuse, and the lack of basic legal rights, highlighting the stark contrast between the laborers' misery and the **hedonistic lifestyle** of the British managers like **Reggie Hunt**.
 
• The novel concludes tragically with the murder of **Gangu** by **Reggie Hunt**, followed by a trial that results in the acquittal of the British officer, thereby illustrating the systematic **injustice** and **racial bias** of the colonial legal system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mulk Raj Anand (1905–2004):**

 
 
• He was a prominent **Indian writer** in English and a pioneer of the **Indo-Anglian novel**, alongside R.K. Narayan and Raja Rao.
 
• Anand was a founding member of the **Progressive Writers' Association** and was deeply influenced by **Marxist ideology** and **social realism**.
 
• His other notable works include **Untouchable (1935)**, which explores the life of a sweeper named **Bakha**, and **Coolie (1936)**, which depicts the struggles of a young hill boy named **Munoo** across various urban labor settings.
 
• He was honored with the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in 1971 and the **Padma Bhushan** in 1967 for his contributions to literature and education.

questions.question: Which of the following reports is associated with Human Development?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Human Development Report**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Human Development Report (HDR)** is an annual publication released by the **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** to measure and analyze global progress in human welfare.
 
• It was first introduced in **1990** by the visionary Pakistani economist **Mahbub ul Haq** and Indian Nobel laureate **Amartya Sen** with the goal of shifting the focus of development economics from national income accounting to people-centered policies.
 
• The report is primarily known for the **Human Development Index (HDI)**, a composite statistic that ranks countries based on three key dimensions: **Long and healthy life** (measured by life expectancy at birth), **Knowledge** (measured by mean and expected years of schooling), and **A decent standard of living** (measured by **Gross National Income (GNI)** per capita).
 
• Unlike traditional economic reports that focus solely on **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)**, the **HDR** explores critical themes such as poverty, gender inequality, and sustainability to provide a holistic view of human capability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Global Risks Report**:

 
 
• This is an annual study published by the **World Economic Forum (WEF)** ahead of its annual meeting in **Davos**.
 
• It identifies and assesses the most significant threats the world faces, categorized into environmental, societal, geopolitical, and technological risks.
 
 
 
• **World Economic Outlook (WEO)**:
 
 
• Published by the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**, this report provides a detailed analysis of the global economy and forecasts future growth trends.
 
• It is released twice a year, typically in **April** and **October**, and serves as a vital resource for global policy coordination.
 
 
 
• **Global Competitiveness Report**:
 
 
• Another flagship publication of the **World Economic Forum (WEF)**, it measures the **Global Competitiveness Index (GCI)**.
 
• It evaluates factors like institutional quality, infrastructure, and market efficiency to determine the level of productivity of various nations.

__
 
• The **Global Energy Transition Index (ETI)** is a specialized framework designed to track and benchmark the progress of various nations toward a **secure, sustainable, and affordable** energy future.
 
• It is published annually by the **World Economic Forum (WEF)**, typically in collaboration with **Accenture**, providing a data-driven analysis for policymakers and business leaders.
 
• The index evaluates countries across two primary dimensions: **Energy System Performance** (current state of the energy system) and **Transition Readiness** (the robustness of the enabling environment for future transitions).
 
• The **System Performance** pillar focuses on three core imperatives: **Environmental Sustainability**, **Energy Security and Access**, and **Economic Development and Growth**.
 
• The **Transition Readiness** dimension measures factors such as **Capital and Investment**, **Regulation and Political Commitment**, **Institutions and Governance**, and **Infrastructure**.
 
• In recent editions, such as the **Energy Transition Index 2024**, advanced economies like **Sweden**, **Denmark**, and **Finland** have consistently ranked at the top of the list.

questions.question: The term 'Upanishads' literally means _____.

• The name reflects the **Guru-Shishya** (teacher-disciple) tradition of ancient India, where students sat at the feet of a master to learn **esoteric knowledge** that was not intended for the general public.

• They are frequently referred to as **Vedanta**, meaning the **end of the Vedas**, signifying the highest goal of Vedic knowledge.
 
• The central theme involves the relationship between **Atman** (the individual soul) and **Brahman** (the universal reality).
 
• Major concepts like **Samsara** (cycle of birth and death), **Karma** (actions), and **Moksha** (liberation) find their primary development in these texts.
 
 
 
• **Important Upanishads:**
 
 
• There are **108 Upanishads** recognized in the **Muktika** canon, though 10 to 13 are considered **Mukhya** (principal) Upanishads.

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of combustion? I. Rapid combustion II. Spontaneous combustion
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rapid combustion** is a process in which a substance burns rapidly and produces a large amount of **heat** and **light** in a very short duration. This occurs when an external source like a spark or a flame is provided, such as the burning of **Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG)** in a kitchen stove or a matchstick catching fire. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Spontaneous combustion** refers to a type of combustion that occurs without the application of any external heat or spark. The substance catches fire on its own when its **ignition temperature** is reached through internal heating or atmospheric conditions. Notable examples include the spontaneous burning of **white phosphorus** at room temperature and devastating fires in **coal mines** caused by coal dust. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other classifications of combustion processes include:
 
 
• **Explosion**: This is a sudden combustion reaction that results in the evolution of heat, light, and a large volume of **gas** accompanied by **sound**. It is commonly observed during the ignition of **firecrackers**.
 
• **Complete Combustion**: Occurs in the presence of **sufficient oxygen**, producing **carbon dioxide** and water. It is characterized by a **non-luminous blue flame**.
 
• **Incomplete Combustion**: Takes place when the **oxygen supply is limited**, leading to the formation of **carbon monoxide**, carbon soot, and water. It is typically identified by a **yellow luminous flame**.
 
• **Ignition Temperature**: The minimum temperature at which a substance catches fire is called its **ignition temperature**; a substance cannot catch fire as long as its temperature is lower than this value.

questions.question: In the context of Indian Budget, which of the following is included in the revenue expenditure?

options.text: Expenditure on acquisition of combat aircraft
Expenditure on acquisition of naval ship

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Subsidies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Revenue Expenditure** consists of all those expenditures of the government which do not result in the creation of physical or financial **assets**. It relates to those expenses that do not reduce the **liabilities** of the government and are typically recurring in nature.
 
• **Subsidies** are a primary component of revenue expenditure in the **Indian Budget**. They are transfer payments made by the government to producers or consumers (such as **Food Subsidies**, **Fertilizer Subsidies**, and **Petroleum Subsidies**) to ensure the affordability of essential goods. These payments are consumed within the fiscal year and provide no direct asset return.
 
• The **Union Budget** classifies expenditures into revenue and capital. Revenue expenditure is essential for the day-to-day running of government machinery and the delivery of **social welfare** services. In recent years, subsidies have accounted for roughly **7% to 9%** of the total revenue expenditure of the **Government of India**.
 
• In contrast, expenditures on **Combat Aircraft**, **Naval Ships**, and **Expressway construction** are classified as **Capital Expenditure** because they involve the acquisition of long-term assets or infrastructure that enhance the nation's productive or defensive capacity over many years.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Capital Expenditure (CapEx)**:

 
 
• **Defense Acquisition**: The procurement of high-value hardware like **fighter jets** and **warships** is recorded under the **Capital Outlay on Defense Services**.
 
• **Infrastructure Development**: The construction of **Expressways** and **National Highways** creates tangible public assets, stimulating long-term economic growth.
 
• **Asset Creation**: Any expenditure that leads to the creation of **machinery**, **equipment**, or **buildings** is categorized here.
 
 
 
• **Other Revenue Expenditure Components**:
 
 
• **Interest Payments**: This is usually the largest single item of revenue expenditure, representing the cost of servicing the **Public Debt**.
 
• **Salaries and Pensions**: Payments made to government employees and retired personnel are mandatory revenue outlays.
 
• **Grants-in-aid**: Grants provided to **State Governments** and **Union Territories** are technically revenue expenditures, even if they are utilized for creating capital assets at the state level.

BODMAS Rule

This acronym defines the priority of operations: **Bracket** (), **Of** (order/powers), **Division** (÷), **Multiplication** (×), **Addition** (+), and **Subtraction** (−).

Priority of Of Operator

Negative Number Rule

questions.question: The LCM of two numbers is 168, and their HCF is 14. If one of the numbers is 42, find the other number.

Product of two numbers = **LCM × HCF**

42 × Second Number = 168 × 14

Second Number = (168 × 14) ÷ 42

Second Number = 168 ÷ 3 = 56

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** = 168

⇒ **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** = 14

⇒ **First Number** (n₁) = 42

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = **LCM** × **HCF**

n₁ × n₂ = LCM(n₁, n₂) × HCF(n₁, n₂)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0f15ee4db0c87022fdaab9074df49ba097096ea2558d38d176b0d2214c5cd20c.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the other number be **x**.

⇒ 42 × x = 168 × 14

⇒ x = (168 × 14) ÷ 42

⇒ x = 2352 ÷ 42

⇒ x = 56

**∴ The correct answer is 56.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF Property

The **Highest Common Factor** of two numbers always divides their **LCM** exactly.

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are **co-prime**, their **HCF is 1** and their **LCM** is equal to the product of the two numbers.

Product Rule Constraint

The formula **Product of Numbers = LCM × HCF** is strictly valid only for **two numbers** and does not apply directly to three or more numbers.

Recognize the algebraic identity: **(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)**.

Here, **a = 5** and **b = √3**.

Sum of squares = 2 × (5² + (√3)²) = 2 × (25 + 3) = 56.

Required value = 56 − 40 = 16.

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ Expansion of (5 + √3)² = 5² + (√3)² + 2 × 5 × √3 = 25 + 3 + 10√3 = **28 + 10√3**

⇒ Expansion of (5 − √3)² = 5² + (√3)² − 2 × 5 × √3 = 25 + 3 − 10√3 = **28 − 10√3**

⇒ Total = (28 + 10√3) + (28 − 10√3) − 40

⇒ Total = 28 + 28 + 10√3 − 10√3 − 40

⇒ Total = 56 − 40

⇒ 16

**∴ The correct answer is 16.**

Standard Algebraic Identities

The identity **(a + b)² + (a − b)² = 2(a² + b²)** is a quick way to sum the squares of binomials with identical terms.

Subtraction of Binomial Squares

Difference of Two Squares

The product of **(a + b)** and **(a − b)** always results in **a² − b²**, which is useful for rationalizing denominators.

questions.question: Which of the following number is divisible by both 3 and 8?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check **Divisibility by 8** first (last three digits) then **Divisibility by 3** (sum of digits).

For **5448**: Last three digits **448** are divisible by **8** (448 ÷ 8 = 56).

Sum of digits **5+4+4+8 = 21**, which is divisible by **3** (21 ÷ 3 = 7).

Both conditions are satisfied for the number **5448**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5448.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers (1) 5448, (2) 5240, (3) 5560, (4) 6170.

**Rules:** A number is divisible by **3** if the **sum of its digits** is divisible by 3. A number is divisible by **8** if the **last three digits** are divisible by 8.

⇒ **Option 1: 5448**

⇒ Sum = 5 + 4 + 4 + 8 = 21 (Divisible by 3 because 21 ÷ 3 = 7)

⇒ Last 3 digits = 448 (Divisible by 8 because 448 ÷ 8 = 56)

⇒ **Option 2: 5240**

⇒ Sum = 5 + 2 + 4 + 0 = 11 (Not divisible by 3)

⇒ **Option 3: 5560**

⇒ Sum = 5 + 5 + 6 + 0 = 16 (Not divisible by 3)

⇒ **Option 4: 6170**

⇒ Sum = 6 + 1 + 7 + 0 = 14 (Not divisible by 3)

**∴ The correct answer is 5448.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 4

A number is divisible by 4 if the number formed by its **last two digits** is divisible by 4 or ends in 00.

Divisibility by 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the **sum of all its digits** is divisible by 9.

Divisibility by 11

The difference between the **sum of digits at odd places** and **even places** must be either 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.question: There is a rectangular garden of 180 metres × 70 metres. A path of width 4 metres is build outside the garden. What is the area (in square metre) of the path?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **path** built **outside** a **rectangular garden**:

Area of path = 2w × (L + B + 2w)

Where L = 180 m, B = 70 m, and w = 4 m.

Area = 2 × 4 × (180 + 70 + 2 × 4) = 8 × (250 + 8)

Area = 8 × 258 = 2064 m².

**∴ The correct answer is 2064 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length (L) of the **rectangular garden** = 180 m

Breadth (B) of the garden = 70 m

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/25c607c04cd65aa1116f2f5b9addf66f04131badfcea1c976116fb87180436a7.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Area of path = (Area including path) − (Area of garden)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Outer Length = 180 + 4 + 4 = 188 m

⇒ Outer Breadth = 70 + 4 + 4 = 78 m

⇒ Inner Area (Garden) = 180 × 70 = 12600 m²

⇒ Outer Area (Total) = 188 × 78 = 14664 m²

⇒ Area of **path** = 14664 − 12600

⇒ Area of **path** = 2064 m²

**∴ The correct answer is 2064 m².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Path Inside a Rectangle

If the path is built inside the rectangular field, the area is calculated as Area = 2w × (L + B − 2w).

Cross-roads Area

Area of two paths of width 'w' crossing each other at right angles in the middle of a field = w × (L + B − w).

Perimeter including Path

The perimeter of the outer boundary after adding a path of width 'w' is 2 × (L + B + 4w).

questions.question: The difference between cost price and selling price of an article is Rs. 720. Loss percentage is 30 percent. What is the selling price of the article?

questions.question: An article is sold for a profit of 50 percent. What is the ratio of the selling price of the article to the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Profit percentage** of 50% can be written as the fraction 1/2.

In this fraction, the denominator represents the **Cost Price (CP)** and the numerator represents the **Profit**.

Let **CP** = 2 units and **Profit** = 1 unit.

**Selling Price (SP)** = **CP** + **Profit** = 2 + 1 = 3 units.

The required **Ratio** of **SP** to **CP** is 3 : 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Profit percentage** = 50%

**Formula Used:**

**Selling Price (SP)** = **Cost Price (CP)** × (100 + **Profit%**) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f5c1394a0f039a23a8672a11bd1bd3af649b9f4ae14bbe5ed824ec40486d30b1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of the article be 100 units.

⇒ **Profit** = 50% of 100 = 50 units.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = **CP** + **Profit**

⇒ **SP** = 100 + 50 = 150 units.

⇒ Required **Ratio** = **SP** : **CP**

⇒ **Ratio** = 150 : 100

⇒ Dividing both sides by 50, we get 3 : 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 : 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Formulas

Successive Discount

Two successive discounts of d₁% and d₂% are equivalent to a single discount of (d₁ + d₂ − d₁d₂/100)%.

questions.question:
Choose the most suitable one-word substitution for the following.
An irrational and intense fear of flying.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aerophobia**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Aerophobia** is defined as the **irrational** and **intense fear** of flying in vehicles such as **airplanes**, **helicopters**, or other **aircraft**.

• The term is etymologically derived from the **Greek** words **'aer'** (air) and **'phobos'** (fear). While it can occasionally refer to a fear of **drafts** or **fresh air**, its primary usage in modern psychology pertains to **aviation**.

• It is classified as a **specific phobia** in the **Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5)** and is often associated with other conditions such as **claustrophobia** or **acrophobia**.

• Physiological symptoms associated with this condition include **tachycardia**, **nausea**, **excessive sweating**, and **panic attacks** occurring before or during a flight.

• This phobia can be addressed through **Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT)**, **exposure therapy**, or the use of **flight simulators** to desensitize the individual to the flying environment.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Acrophobia**:

• Characteristics: It is an extreme or pathological **fear of heights**.

• Applications: It can be triggered by being on **high floors** of buildings, **climbing ladders**, or standing near **cliffs**, often resulting in severe **dizziness** or **vertigo**.

• **Claustrophobia**:

• Characteristics: This is the **fear of enclosed** or **confined spaces**.

• Applications: Common triggers include riding in **elevators**, being in **windowless rooms**, or entering **tunnels**, leading to a sense of being **trapped**.

• **Ophidiophobia**:

• Characteristics: A specific phobia characterized by an abnormal and persistent **fear of snakes**.

• Applications: It is a sub-type of **herpetophobia** and is frequently cited as one of the most common **zoophobias** affecting the human population.

</ul

questions.question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?
The judge advised them to settle the matter amicably.

options.text: They were advised by the judge to settle the matter amicably.
They were advise to settle the matter amicably by the judge.
They were advising by the judge to settle the matter amicably.
The judge advised settling the matter amicably.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They were advised by the judge to settle the matter amicably**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The original sentence is in the **Active Voice** and follows the **Simple Past Tense** structure. The components are **Subject (The judge)**, **Verb (advised)**, **Object (them)**, and an **Infinitive Phrase (to settle the matter amicably)**.

• To convert a **Simple Past** sentence into **Passive Voice**, the object of the active sentence takes the subject position. Here, the pronoun **them** changes to its subjective form **They**.

• The verb form in a passive **Simple Past** sentence changes to **was/were + past participle (V3)**. Since the new subject **They** is plural, the auxiliary **were** is used followed by **advised**.

• The original subject **The judge** becomes the **agent** of the action and is introduced using the preposition **by**.

• The **infinitive complement** (to settle the matter amicably) remains attached to the main verb to complete the meaning of the instruction or advice given.

• Combining these elements results in the structure: **New Subject (They) + were + V3 (advised) + by + Agent (the judge) + Infinitive Phrase**.

 **Additional Information__**

• Analysis of incorrect options:

• **Option 2**: Uses the base form **advise** instead of the **past participle (V3)**. In passive constructions, the main verb must always be in its third form.

• **Option 3**: Employs the **present participle (advising)**, which transforms the sentence into a **Past Continuous** structure, incorrectly implying an ongoing action.

• **Option 4**: This remains in the **Active Voice**. It merely changes the **infinitive** into a **gerund (settling)** but does not shift the focus from the judge to the people being advised.

• **Grammar Rule**: When converting sentences with **Infinitive Complements**, the passive transformation usually focuses on the **finite verb** (advised) while the **non-finite verb** (to settle) stays in its infinitive form.
</ul

</ul

A part of the following sentence is underlined. Choose the option that can replace the underlined part to improve the sentence. If you feel Options A, B, or C do not improve the sentence, then choose Option D: "No improvement required."

After reviewing the proposal, __the team decided to proceed forward with the project__, confident that it would meet the company's goals.

options.text: the team decided to proceed forth with the project
the team decided to proceed with the project
the team decided to proceed onward with the project

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the team decided to proceed with the project**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The primary issue in the original sentence is **redundancy**, specifically a **tautology**. The verb **proceed** inherently means to move forward or to continue a course of action.

• Adding the word **forward** after **proceed** is unnecessary because the direction of the movement is already contained within the definition of the verb itself.

• The phrase **proceed with** is the standard **idiomatic expression** used to indicate the continuation of a task or project without unnecessary modifiers.

• To improve **sentence conciseness** and **grammatical precision**, the redundant adverb must be removed while keeping the preposition **with** to link the action to the object, **the project**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Understanding Redundancy**:

• In English grammar, **pleonasm** occurs when more words than necessary are used to convey a meaning. Common examples include **return back**, **revert back**, or **advance forward**.

• **Analysis of Incorrect Modifiers**:

• **Proceed forth**: The term **forth** means onward or outward. Like **forward**, it repeats the meaning of **proceed** and is considered stylistically weak in formal writing.

• **Proceed onward**: **Onward** specifies movement in a forward direction. Since **proceed** cannot happen backward, this modifier adds no additional information to the sentence.

• **Contextual Usage**:

• While **proceed forward** might be used in casual speech, **academic and professional writing** requires the removal of such fillers to maintain **clarity** and **brevity**.

</ul

questions.question: According to Hans Robert Jauss, why is the final assessment of any literary work considered impossible?

options.text: Because each historical period creates its own horizon of expectations, making meaning change over time

Because interpretation depends solely on authorial intention without considering readers or context
Because literature is disconnected from social history and cultural influences

questions.solution:

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the passage, **Hans Robert Jauss** argues that the meaning of a literary work is deeply tied to its **social history**.
 
• He introduces the concept that every **historical period** establishes its own **'horizon of expectations'**, which dictates how a text is perceived by readers of that time.
 
• Because these expectations change from one era to another, the **overall meaning** of a text is never **fixed** or **universal**.
 
• Since the interpretation is constantly evolving with history, Jauss concludes that the **final assessment** of any literary work is **impossible**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *'As each historical period establishes its own **horizon of expectations**, the overall meaning of the text is not fixed or universal and keeps on changing... thus, the **final assessment** of any literary work becomes **impossible**.'*

 

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2** is incorrect because the passage explicitly states that meanings are **not fixed or universal** and do not remain constant across all eras.
 
• **Option 3** is incorrect because Jauss focuses on the **social history** and the **reader's horizon of expectations** rather than solely on **authorial intention**.
